At the Zama base, where he was assigned around 2009, the base was closed during his tenure, and he was responsible for coordinating the relocation of car carriers and drivers to nearby bases.
Among them were employees who moved to the Sendai CSC, which was in need of personnel at the time.
"With not a single person I knew, there were 50 employees and just me. It was truly a start in the dark."

"I thought about whether we could effectively utilize car carriers across the entire group, rather than just thinking about the Tohoku area. So, I decided to expand our operation area to the Kanto region."

He collaborated with the transportation department at Zero's headquarters to promote initiatives to utilize car carriers that were not being fully utilized in Tohoku in the Kanto region, where cargo volume was high. This is the concept of "overall optimization," effectively utilizing car carriers and drivers across the entire group, not just in the Tohoku area.

While promoting "overall optimization" by utilizing drivers and car carriers across bases, President Ogino has also valued facing each individual working there and engaging in repeated dialogue. He values both thinking about the company as a whole and facing the people working on the front lines.

Unlike in Tohoku, in the Chubu area, while there is a lot of transportation demand, there was the challenge of how to effectively utilize limited drivers and car carriers to reliably transport the cars that have been ordered.

"There is plenty of work. However, it is meaningless if we cannot finish transporting it. We need to think about how to utilize the current drivers and car carriers to properly deliver them to our customers."

That is why President Ogino focused on transportation methods and the operating status of car carriers. He aims to increase transportation efficiency by effectively utilizing car carriers while combining self-driving personnel who transport cars one by one with car carriers that can load multiple cars.
On the other hand, it is not possible to increase the number of necessary car carriers immediately.

"Even if you order new car carriers, it takes a certain amount of time until delivery. On the other hand, there are car carriers that are not operating on days when drivers are off. Rather than just thinking about buying more, I want to first increase the number of drivers who can operate the existing car carriers."

For this reason, he is also working on training drivers who can operate car carriers. By increasing the operation of car carriers that can transport multiple cars at once, he is promoting the creation of a system that can respond to more transportation demand.

"If a package you ordered online with a specified time doesn't arrive, you'd be troubled, right? It's the same with car transportation. Properly delivering the cars entrusted by customers by the promised delivery date. I want to value that obvious thing."

At Zero, human resource development is conducted through training and practical work so that even those without experience can acquire the necessary skills as drivers. President Ogino also values drivers gaining experience in stages and becoming able to handle various car carriers.

"For drivers who have just joined, I have them gain experience with one type of car carrier first, and from there, step up to larger car carriers in stages. In the future, I want to train drivers who can handle various car carriers."
